summary: Aircraft avionics rely on RSA/ECDSA PKI (ARINC 664 networks, flight management systems) with 30–40-year service lives and no practical mid-life crypto retrofit path (RTCA DO-326A/DO-356A airworthiness security processes).

Military and commercial satellite uplinks/downlinks use RSA/ECDSA with 15–25-year operational lifespans; NSA CNSA 2.0 mandates quantum-resistant algorithms for national-security space systems by 2033.
ADS-B broadcasts are unauthenticated and ACARS messaging uses legacy RSA-based protection; ICAO Assembly Resolution A41-19 frames the aviation cybersecurity obligations these links fall under.

Vehicle-to-everything messages are signed with ECDSA P-256 under IEEE 1609.2 certificate hierarchies; a PQC amendment for V2X is in progress while ISO/SAE 21434 governs the vehicle cybersecurity lifecycle.

use_case_label: ECU secure boot & OTA update signing
summary: ECU firmware verification and over-the-air update signing chains use RSA/ECDSA today; hash-based (LMS) and ML-DSA signing are the candidate replacements for long-lived vehicle platforms whose cybersecurity lifecycle ISO/SAE 21434 governs.

Connected-car telematics and OTA delivery ride on TLS where hybrid ML-KEM key establishment is already deployable; UNECE R155/R156 make cybersecurity and software-update management type-approval requirements.
In-vehicle Ethernet security, CAN authentication, and automotive HSM key storage rely on classical ECC with no deployed PQC path yet.
Cloud key-management services, BYOK/HYOK import, and secrets management wrap keys under RSA/ECDH; KEM-based wrapping is arriving through PKCS#11 v3.2 and KMIP profile work.
main_source: Cloud Security Alliance — A Practitioner's Guide to Post-Quantum Cryptography

summary: Hyperscaler front doors terminate TLS for tenant workloads; hybrid X25519+ML-KEM key establishment is in production across major clouds, and NIST IR 8547 frames the federal transition expectations.

use_case_label: Cloud HSM root keys & FIPS modules
summary: Cloud HSM root keys, tenant isolation keys, and FIPS 140-3 module boundaries anchor on RSA/ECDSA; PQC key types are entering validated modules (NIST SP 800-210 covers cloud access-control expectations).
Backup key wrapping, archival storage TLS, and cross-region replication carry harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure because archived ciphertext outlives the classical keys protecting it.
main_source: Cloud Security Alliance — A Practitioner's Guide to Post-Quantum Cryptography

summary: Power-system communications secured per IEC 62351 (RSA-based SCADA authentication, ECDSA in IEC 61850 GOOSE/MMS, DNP3 Secure Authentication) have no standardized PQC profile yet.
Nuclear safety-system digital I&C and safeguards data encryption fall under NRC 10 CFR 73.54 cybersecurity requirements; the cryptography is classical and long-lived.
Advanced metering infrastructure meshes, smart-meter PKI, and PMU authentication use device certificates that must survive multi-decade field deployments.
main_source: University of Toronto Smart Grid Security Research

summary: Pipeline monitoring and OT remote access ride IPsec/IKEv2 VPNs where post-quantum key mixing (RFC 8784) and multiple key exchanges (RFC 9370) are already standardized.

TLS is the universal transport protection for web and API traffic in every sector; hybrid X25519+ML-KEM key establishment is deployed at internet scale, and NIST IR 8547 sets the classical deprecation trajectory.
X.509 certificate hierarchies (roots, intermediates, issuance protocols) run on RSA/ECDSA; ML-DSA and SLH-DSA certificate profiles are advancing through IETF LAMPS.
S/MIME signing and encryption use RSA/ECC via CMS; KEM-based CMS (RFC 9629) and composite ML-KEM/ML-DSA drafts define the migration path.

Code-signing roots, transparency logs, and firmware signing use RSA/ECDSA; hash-based signatures (LMS/SLH-DSA) and ML-DSA are the standardized replacements, with supply-chain frameworks (SLSA) raising the integrity bar.
Enterprise VPNs (IPsec/IKEv2, WireGuard) depend on classical key exchange; NIST SP 800-227 sets KEM usage recommendations and IKEv2 already has standardized post-quantum extensions.
Bitcoin and most chains sign transactions with secp256k1 ECDSA; P2PK outputs and any address whose public key is revealed on first spend are directly quantum-exposed.
Institutional custody stacks keep secp256k1 keys in HSMs with RSA/ECDH key wrapping; the Federal Reserve's HNDL analysis covers the RSA/ECDSA/ECDH exposure across blockchain infrastructure.
main_source: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Paper September 2025

summary: Proof-of-stake consensus and account abstraction roadmaps (Ethereum) contemplate post-quantum signature migration, but BLS/ECDSA remain in production today.
Student records protected under FERPA ride TLS between SIS/LMS platforms and browsers; hybrid key establishment is available wherever the platform's TLS stack is current.
Research-and-education federations sign SAML metadata with RSA-4096 and authenticate eduroam via certificate-based EAP; no PQC profile is deployed in the federation trust fabric yet.
main_source: Internet2 InCommon Federation / Jisc Trust and Identity

summary: W3C Verifiable Credentials envelope academic credentials in JOSE/COSE signatures (ECDSA/EdDSA/RSA-PSS); PQ/T composite signature drafts for JOSE/COSE define the upgrade path.
Controlled unclassified research data falls under NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3; repositories and HPC access paths (TLS, SSH) already have hybrid PQC options.
main_source: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 — Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information

summary: SWIFTNet PKI, Fedwire, and Eurosystem T2 settlement authenticate with RSA certificates; BIS Project Leap has demonstrated quantum-safe interbank messaging end to end.
main_source: Bank for International Settlements Project Leap Phase 2

summary: Customer-facing banking apps and portals ride TLS where hybrid ML-KEM is production-ready; FS-ISAC urges coordinated migration timelines across the sector.
main_source: FS-ISAC — The Timeline for Post Quantum Cryptographic Migration

summary: Payment and banking HSAM estates wrap working keys under RSA/ECDH; PCI DSS v4 key-management requirements meet PQC through PKCS#11 v3.2 mechanism support.
Archived financial records and recorded transport sessions are harvest-now-decrypt-later targets; the Federal Reserve's HNDL analysis quantifies the exposure window for the sector.
main_source: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Paper September 2025

summary: NSA CNSA 2.0 mandates ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, and hash-based firmware signing across national security systems, with non-compliant equipment phased out by the early 2030s.
The US Federal PKI issues RSA-2048/4096 and ECDSA P-256/P-384 certificates government-wide; ML-DSA certificate profiles from IETF LAMPS are the designated successors.
Strategic and classified communication systems depend on public-key key establishment whose compromise horizon is measured in decades — the driving case for CNSA 2.0's timeline.
CISA's product-category guidance tells agencies which COTS categories must land PQC support first, making procurement the enforcement point for federal migration.
main_source: CISA Product Categories for PQC Technologies

summary: Electronic health records and HIE transport are protected under the HIPAA Security Rule's encryption specifications; patient data's decades-long sensitivity makes HNDL a first-order risk.
FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance requires secure update mechanisms for devices whose field lives exceed classical-crypto safety margins; hash-based and ML-DSA signing are the migration path.
Implantables and wearables use embedded ECC over Bluetooth LE with severe compute and battery constraints — among the hardest PQC retrofit cases in any sector.
main_source: FDA — DSCSA Standards for the Interoperable Exchange of Information for Tracing (Guidance for Industry, Sept 2023)

summary: US DSCSA interoperability rests on EPCIS event signatures and manufacturer PKI for product verification; signatures anchoring provenance must remain verifiable for years.
main_source: FDA Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA)

summary: HSMs generating ML-KEM/FN-DSA keys need fault and side-channel countermeasures that FIPS 140-3 physical-security requirements were not originally written for.
main_source: NIST FIPS 140-3 Physical Security Requirements / IACR PQC fault attack research

summary: PKCS#11 v3.2 (OASIS Standard) defines mechanisms for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and stateful hash-based signatures — the API layer of the HSM migration is standardized.
Device roots of trust (TPM, UEFI Secure Boot) verify firmware with RSA/ECDSA; hash-based signatures are the recommended first PQC step for firmware because of their conservative security case.
main_source: NIST FIPS 140-3 Physical Security Requirements / IACR PQC fault attack research

summary: IoT device identity rests on factory-provisioned ECDSA/RSA certificates in devices that often cannot be re-keyed after deployment; NIST SP 800-213 and NISTIR 8259A define the device cybersecurity capability baseline this migration runs through.
OPC UA security policies and IEC 62443 conformance anchor industrial device authentication on RSA/ECDSA with multi-decade plant lifecycles.
IETF SUIT (RFC 9019/9124) defines the firmware-update architecture whose COSE signatures must move from ECDSA/EdDSA to PQC for constrained devices.
OpenSSL 3.5 shipped ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA natively, putting PQC into the default dependency graph of most software; legacy pre-3.5 estates are the migration tail.
CA root and intermediate keys (RSA-4096/ECDSA) anchor the web PKI under CA/Browser Forum baseline requirements; ML-DSA certificate profiles are advancing through IETF LAMPS.
Sigstore's Fulcio CA and Rekor transparency log sign with ECDSA; SLSA provenance levels make those signatures the trust anchor for software supply chains.
SAML assertions, OAuth/OIDC tokens (JOSE), and FIDO2/WebAuthn attestation all sign with RSA/ECDSA; the FIDO Alliance has a PQC roadmap and JOSE/COSE composite drafts exist.
main_source: Web Authentication: An API for accessing Public Key Credentials - Level 3

summary: SSH hybrid ML-KEM key exchange is standardized (RFC 9941) and deployed by default in current OpenSSH — administrative access is among the most PQC-ready surfaces in IT.
Qualified signatures under eIDAS use RSA/ECDSA in XAdES/PAdES/CAdES formats with algorithm suites from ETSI TS 119 312; PQC suites are in ETSI's standardization pipeline.
EUDI wallets under Regulation 2024/1183 authenticate holders and verifiers with ECDSA/RSA credentials; wallet attestation formats are where PQC composite signatures will land.
Qualified timestamp tokens (ETSI EN 319 422, RFC 3161) sign evidence of existence whose verifiability must outlast the signing algorithm — a canonical long-validity PQC case.
AACS, PlayReady, and FairPlay rest on RSA key hierarchies burned into devices and discs; content licensing windows outlive the classical hardness assumptions beneath them.
main_source: AACS Specifications — Introduction and Common Cryptographic Elements (v0.91)

summary: DVB conditional-access entitlement management (ECM/EMM) and broadcast device certificates use RSA/ECDSA with fielded receiver populations that are effectively un-upgradable.
main_source: DVB Project — Conditional Access System Standards

summary: Streaming platforms deliver content keys and licenses over TLS, where hybrid PQC key establishment is already available at CDN scale.
main_source: "A First Look at Digital Rights Management Systems for Secure Mobile Content Delivery" (academic survey)

summary: EMV offline card authentication (SDA/DDA/CDA per EMVCo Book 2) uses RSA, with ECDSA arriving in newer contactless kernels; card and terminal fleets turn over on decade timescales.
main_source: The Impact of Quantum Computing on the Payment Card Industry

summary: PIN encryption uses TDES DUKPT with RSA-based remote key injection under PCI PIN Security Requirements; asymmetric key transport is the quantum-exposed link.
Cardholder-data environments protect transport with TLS under PCI DSS v4 requirements; hybrid key establishment is deployable now on the acquiring side.
ETCS online key management (UNISIG SUBSET-137) distributes KMAC keys via RSA/ECDSA-authenticated channels; signalling assets have 30+-year lifecycles.
main_source: UNISIG SUBSET-137 — On-line Key Management FFFIS (KMC-ETCS)
vetting_body: UNISIG; European Union Agency for Railways

summary: FRMCS, the 5G successor to GSM-R, authenticates with ECDSA/RSA under ETSI TS 103 719 and 3GPP profiles; migrating rail radio is a multi-decade infrastructure program.
main_source: ETSI TS 103 764 (FRMCS System Architecture) + ETSI TS 103 765-1/-2 (Transport/Service Stratum) / 3GPP TS 22.289 / TS 23.289

summary: US Positive Train Control mandated by 49 CFR 236 Subpart I relies on PKI-authenticated wireless messaging between locomotives, wayside units, and back offices.
main_source: 49 CFR Part 236 Subpart I — Positive Train Control Systems (eCFR)

summary: Checkout and point-of-sale traffic is TLS under PCI DSS; hybrid ML-KEM is production-ready in modern commerce stacks.
Port management PKI, vessel identity certificates, and maritime VPNs fall under IMO cyber-risk management guidance; fleet IT refresh cycles are long.
main_source: IMO Maritime Cyber Risk Management Guidelines

use_case_label: Electronic bills of lading & trade docs
summary: DCSA electronic bill-of-lading standards sign trade documents with RSA/ECDSA; negotiable instruments demand signature validity across multi-year disputes.
main_source: DCSA Electronic Bill of Lading Standards

summary: Customs single-window platforms and AEO certificates under the WCO SAFE framework authenticate declarations with classical digital signatures.
5G SUCI conceals subscriber identifiers with ECIES (Curve25519/P-256); 3GPP study items and NIST CSWP 36A chart the ML-KEM-based replacement.
Inter-site N2/N3 IPsec and SBA TLS carry the mobile core; GSMA's PQ.03 guidelines sequence the telco network migration and IKEv2 PQ extensions are standardized.
3GPP TS 33.310 certificate profiles for network functions and base stations use RSA/ECDSA today; ML-DSA profiles track the LAMPS certificate work.
Legacy generations and roaming interconnects still depend on classical asymmetric authentication and key exchange flagged in GSMA security guidance.
Water utility SCADA authentication and remote-monitoring VPNs fall under America's Water Infrastructure Act assessments; OT asset lifecycles stretch decades.
main_source: EPA America's Water Infrastructure Act (AWIA) 2018 / CISA

summary: Smart water meters and sensor-to-gateway bootstrap use RSA/ECC provisioning per EPA water-sector cybersecurity guidance.
FERC's hydropower security program covers certificate-based remote access to dam control systems — classical VPN cryptography guarding kinetic infrastructure.
main_source: FERC Security Program for Hydropower Projects

summary: Insurers hold decades-sensitive policyholder and claims data behind TLS and classically-encrypted stores; Munich Re's 2025 cyber-trends report flags harvest-now-decrypt-later theft and the NIST PQC transition (RSA vulnerable to quantum decryption, protection horizon ~2030) as a sector concern.
main_source: Munich Re — Cyber Insurance: Risks and Trends 2025 (quantum computing security section)

summary: Cyber insurers carry accumulation exposure if a cryptographically relevant quantum computer breaks the RSA/ECDSA protecting their insureds en masse; Munich Re's 2025 cyber-trends report treats the PQC transition as an underwriting-relevant risk trend.
main_source: Munich Re — Cyber Insurance: Risks and Trends 2025 (quantum computing security section)

use_case_label: Mastercard PQC industry awareness (payment ecosystem quantum-migration whitepaper)
summary: Mastercard's 2025 R&D white paper (verified 2026-07-31 from the downloaded PDF). Frames HNDL as the central driver and compares PQC against Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) as the two quantum-safe technology categories, favoring PQC for deployability. Cites industry-wide TLS 1.3 PQC adoption data from Cloudflare (nearly 2% of connections by March 2024, reaching double digits by end of 2024) as evidence of momentum -- this is an internet-wide statistic the paper quotes, not a claim about Mastercard's own network. States no QKD trial or pilot of its own. Its concrete recommendation to financial institutions is to invest in cryptographic inventory tooling now, 'regardless of the timeline for PQC migration that it deems to be ideal' -- the paper does not commit to a specific readiness timeline (no 3- or 5-year figure appears in the text).
